independent_argument.finite_trace_to_set_packing: For every finite eta-separated set subfamily of size m, iid Q points distinguish every pair with positive probability when n=ceil(2 log(m)/eta). Union bound over pair coincidences gives probability <=m(m-1)/2 *exp(-n eta)<1. Trace size is then >=m and <=sum_{j<=S}binomial(n,j). Wellner uses binomial <=(en/S)^S for S>=1,n>=S (elementary generating-function bound with t=S/n); combining yields m<=[K eta^-1 log(3e/eta)]^S, K=3e^2/(e-1). Apply to arbitrary finite separated families, not an assumed attained/infinite packing number; bounded packing yields a finite maximal net. S=0 is a singleton-equivalence class and handled separately.
independent_argument.envelope_transfer: Let M=Q(F^r) in (0,infinity), F>=0. On D={(x,t):|t|<=F(x)}, define probability P(dx dt)=F(x)^(r-1) Q(dx) dt/(2M), using density 1 for r=1, and 0 at F=0 for r>1. Fubini gives P(C_f triangle C_g)=Q[F^(r-1)|f-g|]/(2M). As |f-g|<=2F, ||f-g||_{Q,r}^r/M <=2^r P(C_f triangle C_g). Restricting subgraphs to D does not increase VC dimension S=V-1. Therefore an eta=(epsilon/2)^r set cover supplies an epsilon ||F||_{Q,r} function cover; Q-null infinite envelope values may be discarded. Finite Q F^r gives a finite probability normalization, including r=1. This yields the exact repaired logarithmic display.
independent_argument.universal_power_bound: For x=3e/eta>1, log x<=x. Thus set bound <=(3e K eta^-2)^S=[3e K (2/epsilon)^(2r)]^S. Since r>=1, this is <=(32/epsilon)^(2rS): 32^2>=4*3e*K. It is consequently <=(32/epsilon)^(32rV), giving a universal A=32 for the simpler requested form. The logarithmic bound retained in the scaffold is stronger and fully supported by the proved source route.
independent_argument.why_old_clause_false: Take Q uniform on [0,1], envelope 1, f_t(x)=1{x<=t}, t in [0,1]. The subgraph VC dimension is 1 (source index V=2), while ||f_t-f_s||_r=|t-s|^(1/r). Grid spacing (3epsilon)^r gives more than c_r epsilon^-r functions pairwise >2epsilon apart, so any epsilon-cover has >=c_r epsilon^-r members, even with arbitrary centers. For any proposed universal A, choose finite r>2A; as epsilon tends to 0 this contradicts (A/epsilon)^(2A). The failure has no measurability or envelope loophole.
